sections.title: 19 October follow-up: the blocked career now continues
paragraphs: The original 39-match run remains recorded below. It ended at Season 3, Week 5. It did not beat D1 or the Hero Cup.
After the local fixes, I reopened that same saved career in the muted background browser. Quick Match completed s3-r1-m1 as a 4–2 win over Ulric Rockets.
The career advanced to Season 3, Week 6, with $40,312 and 49 TP. A full reload kept the result. This is one additional real browser match.

The coach cards now include the Level 2 Coaching Office bonus: Nia Thompson's stored Level 2/$600 candidate showed Level 3/$900 head wage and $450 assistant wage. Both roles were occupied, so I did not perform a new browser hire. Focused tests verify the actual head and assistant hire wages.
The rookie creation screen showed $153/week on a separate fresh origin. All seven catalogs use the real wage value.

In a separate UI fixture, the One big night out refusal showed 7 loyalty and 11 morale for the asker, plus 2 loyalty and 3 morale for every other player. Clicking Refuse changed Ken Ash from 65 to 58 loyalty and 64 to 53 morale. This fixture is not career progress.

Grok reviewed the report and fixes. I accepted the confirmed fixes, kept intentional REF display behavior, and deferred academy resale balance changes. Muse and Opus were unavailable because their providers reported usage limits.

Grok caught three checkpoint tool edge cases. The final check covers missing careers, codec failures, engine differences, unavailable matches, and opening-match power removal. His earlier Quick Match energy claim was corrected: only the opponent receives automatic energy changes in a user-controlled Quick Match.

Passed: 206 focused Jest tests across 12 suites; TypeScript; the permanent tool self-check; the captured blocker check; and read-only checkpoint validation with one production-engine simulation. No scoreline goldens, balance changes, new dependencies, commits, pushes, or releases were added.

The permanent tools are scripts/qa/playtest-browser.js and scripts/qa/check-career.cjs. The read-only bridge requires a local ?qa=playtest URL. AGENTS.md points to docs/qa/game-playtest.md. Phone, Tailscale, and Practice Battle instructions belong to the user's other game and were excluded.

Limits: D1 and Hero Cup wins remain unproved. No phone, native, Steam, audible audio, or physical-device performance test was performed. A team with too few legal available players can still be refused; the optional preload now lets the title recover.

sections.title: Original run: blocked in Season 3, not beaten
paragraphs: I completed two seasons, 39 matches, and 290 instant drills. I earned promotion from D5, then finished third in D4.
The run stopped at Season 3, Week 5. Selling Sol Reed caused an AI lineup error before the first league match.
Back to Title and a full page reload both returned to the same error. I did not win D1 or the Hero Cup.
The best next strategy is to build income early, buy strong starters, and train pace sooner. The later-game plan below remains unproved in this run.

sections.title: What was tested
paragraphs: Career seed: 3521330691. Difficulty: Chairman. Club: Bramble Rovers. Created player: Ace, a forward.
Source baseline: 17577f73205890dd20fc1a935c75c036e8e0b1ed. Engine: m2.9. The run started on 18 October and ended on 19 October 2026, Vietnam time.
I used the background Paseo browser at 900 × 600. The built-in IAB surface was unavailable. Game volume stayed at zero, with media guards installed.
Career actions used rendered controls. Store access was read-only for inspection. No stats, cash, results, or saves were injected.
Most matches used Quick Match. Two matches were watched at 3× speed. No match result was rerolled.
Concurrent work changed the main checkout during Season 2. I moved the server to a detached baseline checkout with locked dependencies.
The same browser origin retained the career. There is a UI-log gap around that reload. The saved match records and drill counter remained available.
No game source changes were made during the original run. The dated follow-up records later local fixes. No commits, pushes, or releases were made.

sections.title: Career results
paragraphs: League results total 36 matches. The three Cup matches were a 0–3 loss, a 2–0 win, and a 0–8 loss.
Season 1: second place earned promotion. Ace scored 12 league goals.
Season 2: Ben Stone scored 25 league goals. The team improved its attack but missed promotion.
The two clubs relegated from D3 took the promotion places. This run also contained training and recruitment mistakes.
The clearest watched success was a 7–0 win over Zircon Casuals. I used 3-4-3, Attack, and Save Energy.

sections.title: Money spent and decisions made
paragraphs: I invested $221,000 in facilities: $124,500 in new buildings and $96,500 in upgrades.
I bought four Tier 2 drill paths for $20,000. Scouting cost $10,250 across four missions.
Transfer fees totalled $43,769. Player sales returned $76,308, including the Sol Reed sale that later blocked the career.
I kept two licensed heroes: Ace with Portal Pass and Ed Stone with Web Trap.
I hired Mei Chen as head coach and Rafael Costa as assistant. Their actual wages were $900 and $300 weekly.
The final training supply was 44 TP each week: 10 base, 24 from the Training Pitch, and 10 from coaches.

sections.title: Facilities at the stopping point
paragraphs: All 12 facility types were built. The club owned 16 buildings, with all three adjacency combinations active.
The combinations were Fan Shop + Stadium Stand, Gym + Dorm, and Medical Bay + Training Pitch.
No construction was unfinished at the crash. Weekly upkeep was $1,435.

sections.title: The strategy I would use on the next attempt
bullets: Build the Training Pitch first. Then unlock the assistant through the Coaching Office. Their early TP keeps producing gains all season.
Build extra Level 1 Fan Shops and Stadium Stands before expensive commercial upgrades. A new stand adds 100 percentage points for $10,000. Its first upgrade adds 50 for $25,000.
Keep about four weeks of net non-match spending in cash. This squad needed roughly $14,000 after merchandise income. My earlier $1,577 low point was too risky.
Buy a strong starting goalkeeper and a fast forward before buying every support facility. Keep a spare goalkeeper and usable outfield cover.
Prioritize young starters, useful role stats, and pace. Do not keep raising DEF while the same defender cannot reach a runner.
Goalkeeper REF includes an intentional display bonus. Compare match performance when judging keepers. Changing the display needs an owner decision.
Train pace much earlier. The sampled Bramble XI had median PAC 62. Hollow Union and Ashford Olympic had 98 and 99.
Use the best legal natural-role XI. Keep 4-4-2 while only two forwards are strong. Consider 4-3-3 or 3-4-3 after a strong third forward arrives.
Use Quick Match against weaker teams for speed. Watch close promotion and Cup matches when changing energy or playstyle can matter.
In watched matches, test Save Energy first. Avoid using All-out for the whole match. The measured policy advantage is limited to the sampled teams.
Send scouts early enough to return during Weeks 1–4 or 17–18. A position-specific brief can take four weeks. Check its exact arrival week.
Use three-year contracts for affordable core players. Use Starter promises only for players who should remain first choice.
Keep hero capacity available for useful awakenings. In this source version, avoid selling heroes until the AI lineup bug is fixed.
Answer player requests before their deadline. Squad requests can affect everyone, including the asker. The current refusal text understates that cost.

sections.title: What I would change in my own play
bullets: I spread TP into the backup goalkeeper and overdeveloped defensive stats. I should have fixed starting pace and stamina sooner.
I built every support facility to exercise the system. A pure speed run should delay the less useful ones.
I did not finish the D4 rebuild before the first transfer window closed. That helped cost a season.
The Season 3 MID mission showed a four-week duration. I sent it in Week 1 anyway. Missing the opening window was my mistake.
The 7–0 watched win does not prove that 3-4-3 always wins. Later Quick Match losses showed that it does not.
This was one adaptive career, not an optimized run across many career seeds. I cannot claim a minimum season count.

sections.title: Tactics check: 648 separate headless matches
paragraphs: I tested three formations, two playstyles, and three energy settings against three captured opponents. Each combination used 12 seeds.
These are production-engine simulations, separate from the browser career. They did not change the saved game.
The fixed Season 2 squad played at home against Hollow Union, Ashford Olympic, and Zircon Casuals.
Across this sample, Save Energy kept more condition and earned more points. All-out performed worst.
The best single formation/playstyle/energy group was 4-4-2, Attack, Balanced: 24 wins, four draws, and eight losses across 36 games.
That group averaged 2.11 points. Different opponents favored different settings. This is not proof of a universal best tactic.
Quick Match only receives the formation preference from the UI. It uses automatic powers and substitutions. Watched energy changes do not carry into Quick Match.

sections.title: Balance observations that need more evidence
bullets: Commercial buildings were strong investments. Season 2 produced $176,491 in tickets and $71,645 in merchandise. Wages plus upkeep cost $138,285.
This does not prove that money is too easy. I repeatedly ran low on cash, and D3–D1 has additional costs.
Relegated stronger clubs can make the next division feel uneven. Recheck this across career seeds with a better recruitment policy.
Save Energy beat All-out in the fixed tactics sample. Test away matches, late substitutions, and other squad strengths before changing balance.
The browser logged repeated WebGL context-limit warnings during the long session. I did not prove a leak or connect them to a match failure.
The earlier reload happened during concurrent source and dependency changes. It is separate from the reproducible sold-hero failure.

sections.title: D3–D1 plan: code-backed, not reached in this run
bullets: D3 grants the third hero slot and unlocks Tier 3 drills. Rebuild weak positions before committing to a costly marquee hero.
Check Green Bull before individual drills. It starts at $50,000, consumes the whole TP bank, and gives the squad +2 to stored attributes.
Green Bull adds $25,000 per prior visit for the first ten increases, then $50,000. Its value depends on the roster and cash reserve.
D3 also unlocks banked coach speeches for watched matches. A speech consumes the TP bank and gives +6 second-half attributes; D2 gives +8 and D1 +10.
D2 unlocks Level 3 facilities. Upgrade the TP engine and commercial output before lower-priority facilities.
D1 grants the fourth hero slot. The main journey requires both the D1 title and the Hero Cup.
Watch decisive matches when tactical controls can change the result. Preserve healthy cover for shared league and Cup weeks.
This run did not exercise D3–D1 management, Green Bull bookings, the D1 title, or the Cup ending. No endgame win is claimed.

sections.title: Behaviors I did not count as bugs
bullets: Quick Match uses automatic powers and substitutions. That is intentional.
The first-match tutorial delays automatic substitutions until the lesson is introduced.
The short confirmation guard can ignore a very fast second press. Automation must wait for the guard.
Drill presentations are skippable, and consecutive drills already exist. Repeated manual viewing is not required.
Wins in recent form use trophy art. Missing letter W text alone is not missing match history.
Starter promises constrain lineup changes. Those constraints were disclosed when signing.

sections.title: Original-run verification and limits
paragraphs: Passed: four focused Jest suites, 106 tests. The tests cover instant training, midseason training, market careers, and career persistence.
Passed: npx tsc --noEmit on the pinned baseline. The command returned exit code 0 with no diagnostic output.
Passed: the 648-match tactics probe, including deterministic repeat and unchanged input checks.
Failed as expected: reproduce-career-blocker.cjs returned exit code 1 on the baseline and main checkout. Both printed the exact sold-hero error.
The existing passing tests do not cover this AI selection failure. The reproduction script preserves a small regression check for it.
Browser coverage was desktop web, with silent audio. No physical iPhone, PWA, native, audible audio, or Steam performance claim is made.
The QA page was destroyed and closed. The QA server was stopped. The listener audit found no remaining Hero Football Manager listener.
No game fixes occurred during the original run. Later fixes are in the dated follow-up. Unrelated dirty files were preserved, and nothing was published.

findings.title: Selling a hero can block the whole career
findings.observed: I sold unlicensed Sol Reed to Dunwich Panthers for $35,163 in S3 W1. At S3 W5, the screen failed with: Hero bramble-rovers-p15 must be licensed or benched.
findings.impact: No match controls or title screen remained usable. The buyer was in a different fixture. Back to Title and a full reload repeated the error.
findings.cause: Sales set licensed to false. The AI freshness picker admits unlicensed heroes. It chose Sol despite his absence from the saved starting XI. Rival preload then built an invalid team.
findings.fix: Exclude unlicensed heroes from AI selection. Cover hero sales with a regression check. Also prevent rival preload from trapping the title and crash recovery screens.
findings.evidence: Browser screenshot 04; captured crashCareer; blocker-check.txt. The same check also failed against the main checkout. Excluding Sol through an existing availability rule on a copy removed the error.
findings.currentVerification: Same save completed 4–2, reached S3 W6, and survived reload.

findings.title: Displayed REF can reverse the apparent ranking of two goalkeepers
findings.observed: At S2 W21, Jae Gray showed REF 210 but stored 102. Leo Knox showed 201 but stored 145.
findings.impact: The weaker keeper appears stronger on the card. Training decisions can follow a value that the match engine never uses.
findings.cause: refDisplayBonus intentionally banks a visual-only training bonus. Match selection, transfer valuation, and the engine use attrs.ref.
findings.fix: Show the actual match stat and actual drill gain. If a separate development score is wanted, name and explain it separately. Treat any migration as a distinct design task.
findings.evidence: evidence.json finding reflexes-display. This is deliberate code behavior, reported as a design problem rather than an accidental sim defect.
findings.currentVerification: REF display bonus is intentional. No display or balance change.

findings.title: Coach hire confirmation understates the actual wage
findings.observed: With Coaching Office L2, Mei Chen was quoted at $600/week and Level 2. Hiring produced Level 3 at $900/week. The same office-bonus code can raise an assistant wage from $150 to $300/week. A separate captured assistant quote was not found.
findings.impact: The player approves one recurring cost and receives another. The hire celebration also uses the old level and effects.
findings.cause: The transaction applies the office level bonus and recomputes wages. The quote and celebration use the candidate before that adjustment.
findings.fix: Calculate one effective hire quote. Use its level, effects, and wage in affordability checks, confirmation, and the hire result.
findings.evidence: evidence.json finding coach-hire-quote captures the $600 confirmation and the actual $900 coach.
findings.currentVerification: Shared arrival quote; rendered bonus level/wage; head and assistant hire tests passed.

findings.title: Squad request refusal hides the real penalties
findings.observed: Ken Ash asked for One big night out in S2 W28. Refuse advertised −5 loyalty and −8 morale. Ken actually lost 7 and 11. Every other player lost 2 and 3.
findings.impact: The choice hides a whole-squad cost and understates the asking player’s loss.
findings.cause: resolutionDeltas adds asker and squad deltas. The view model prints only asker deltas.
findings.fix: Show the asking player’s total change and the other players’ change. Use the same calculation for refusal and lapse warnings.
findings.evidence: evidence-segment-2.json finding request-refusal-omits-squad-cost contains every before/after delta.
findings.currentVerification: Shared full-cost copy in card and lapse warning; UI refusal matched asker cost; both difficulty tests passed.

findings.title: An academy signing produced immediate cash profit
findings.observed: I signed Kai Stone for $500 in S2 W1, then immediately sold him for $5,776. Profit was $5,276 before any training, match, or week advance.
findings.impact: A cheap intake can become a cash conversion rather than a player development choice.
findings.cause: The low signing fee and ordinary transfer valuation allow an immediate profitable sale when squad cover permits it.
findings.fix: Decide whether this is intended. Options include an initial resale discount or a short registration period. Do not remove normal academy development profits.
findings.evidence: Cash transactions 17 and 18, and evidence.json finding academy-resale-confirmed. Verified once; not an unlimited-money claim.
findings.currentVerification: One profitable academy sale does not establish an unlimited money exploit.

findings.title: Created-player wage copy still says $180
findings.observed: The creation card showed $180/week. Ace entered the career on $153/week.
findings.impact: The first contract does not match the terms shown during creation.
findings.cause: Creation uses reducedPlayerWeeklyWage(180), while the English text still hardcodes 180.
findings.fix: Format the terms from the actual creation wage. Check all language catalogs.
findings.evidence: Ace’s first captured roster and the creation text. The actual wage is lower, so this does not overcharge the player.
findings.currentVerification: Rookie wage comes from the real constant; browser displayed $153.

findings.title: The drill guide disagrees with the shipped Tier 5 ladder
findings.observed: The guide says +20 outfield and +11 keeper at Tier 5. The captured rules ship +18 and +10.
findings.impact: The guide also promises rising efficiency. Raw outfield gain falls from 13/26 = 0.500 per TP to 18/39 = 0.462.
findings.cause: The canonical guide did not follow the current content values.
findings.fix: Reconcile the guide and content after deciding the intended ladder. Show the real tradeoff before the $60,000 upgrade.
findings.evidence: crashCareer.trainingRules and docs/05. This was checked in code, not purchased in this career. Modifiers and SUPER can affect realized value.
findings.currentVerification: Tier 5 +18/+10 and lower raw efficiency documented. Training rules unchanged.

findings.title: Generic scouting copy omits four-week missions
findings.observed: The board says reports take two or three weeks. A position-specific mission can take four. My S3 W1 MID mission was due in Week 5.
findings.impact: Generic advice can lead to a missed transfer window. The exact mission slip does show its duration.
findings.cause: Duration is two or three weeks plus one for a role-specific profile. The generic text omits that extra week.
findings.fix: Say two to four weeks. Showing the arrival week beside the registration deadline would also help.
findings.evidence: The captured active mission ran from absolute week 61 to 65. Sending it too late was my mistake, not a hidden duration change.
findings.currentVerification: Generic scouting text says 2–4 weeks in all seven catalogs. Exact mission slips unchanged.
